subject: maths
title: Reading Scales and Temperature
seo_title: Year 4 Reading Scales and Temperature Worksheets (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Interpret unmarked and partial units when measuring and comparing attributes of length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature, using scaled and digital instruments
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on reading scales: rulers and tape measures, kitchen and bathroom scales, measuring jugs, thermometers in °C (including below zero) and stopwatches, with unlabelled marks. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Count the spaces between two numbers to find what one mark is worth.
key_sub: Jump ÷ spaces = one mark. Start at 0, count on from the number before, and write a minus sign for temperatures below zero.
body_html:
Find what one mark is worth

Most marks on a scale have no number. Before you read it, work out what one mark is worth.

1. Find two numbers next to each other. 2. Count the spaces between them (not the marks). 3. Divide: the jump ÷ the number of spaces.

Numbers go up bySpaces betweenEach mark is worth
10 cm510 ÷ 5 = 2 cm
200 g4200 ÷ 4 = 50 g
1 kg (1000 g)41000 ÷ 4 = 250 g
1 L (1000 mL)101000 ÷ 10 = 100 mL
10 °C1010 ÷ 10 = 1 degree

Rulers: start at 0

If an object does not start at 0, take the start away from the end.

Scales and jugs

If the needle or water is halfway between two marks, the answer is halfway between their values. Halfway between 500 mL and 600 mL is 550 mL.

Thermometers and temperatures below zero

We measure temperature in degrees Celsius (°C). Water freezes at 0 °C. A temperature below zero has a minus sign: −2 °C is 2 degrees colder than 0 °C.

Stopwatches

An analog stopwatch goes once around in 60 seconds. A digital stopwatch shows minutes, then a colon, then seconds: 01:25 is 1 min 25 s. Remember 1 min = 60 s.

Compare

Which is heavier: 1 kg 500 g or 1300 g?

Change to the same unit: 1 kg 500 g = 1500 g. 1500 g is more than 1300 g.

Answer: 1 kg 500 g

How much warmer?

It is −2 °C in the morning and 12 °C in the afternoon.

From −2 °C up to 0 is 2 degrees. From 0 up to 12 is 12 degrees. 2 + 12 = 14.

Answer: 14 degrees

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the marks instead of the spacesCount the spaces (jumps) between two numbers
Thinking every mark is worth 1Work out what one mark is worth first: jump ÷ spaces
Reading the end of an object that does not start at 0Take the start away from the end
Reading −2 °C as 2 °CBelow 0, count back from 0 and write the minus sign
Reading 01:25 on a stopwatch as 1 hour 25 minutes or 125 secondsIt is 1 min 25 s, and 1 min = 60 s, so 85 s

faq.q: What does Year 4 measurement cover in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 4 students read scaled and digital instruments where not every mark is labelled, including rulers, tape measures, kitchen and bathroom scales, jugs, thermometers in °C and stopwatches, and they compare length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature.

faq.q: How do you read a scale with unlabelled marks?
faq.a: Find two numbers next to each other, count the spaces between them and divide the jump by the number of spaces. That tells you what each mark is worth, so you can count on from the number before.

faq.q: Do Year 4 students learn negative temperatures?
faq.a: Yes, in a simple way. They read thermometers in °C, including temperatures just below zero such as −2 °C, which is 2 degrees colder than 0 °C.

faq.q: Is reading scales tested in NAPLAN?
faq.a: Year 4 does not sit NAPLAN, but reading scales and instruments is part of the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test, so Year 4 is a good time to practise it.

sets.title: Rulers and tape measures with unlabelled marks

items.q: On a ruler, how many small spaces are there from 3 cm to 4 cm?
items.e: There are 9 small marks between 3 and 4, but 10 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks. Each space is 1 mm, and 10 mm = 1 cm.
It starts at 0. It ends 7 small spaces past 4 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 4 cm 7 mm = 47 mm.
It starts at 0. It ends 2 small spaces past 6 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 6 cm 2 mm = 62 mm.
It starts at 0. It ends 5 small spaces past 8 cm. Each small space is 1 mm, so it is 8 cm 5 mm = 85 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 20 mm and ends at 58 mm. 58 − 20 = 38 mm, which is 3 cm 8 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 30 mm and ends at 74 mm. 74 − 30 = 44 mm, which is 4 cm 4 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 15 mm and ends at 52 mm. 52 − 15 = 37 mm, which is 3 cm 7 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 40 mm and ends at 96 mm. 96 − 40 = 56 mm, which is 5 cm 6 mm.
It does not start at 0. It starts at 25 mm and ends at 70 mm. 70 − 25 = 45 mm, which is 4 cm 5 mm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 10 = 1 cm. Count the spaces after 140 cm: 141 cm, 142 cm, 143 cm. So it is 143 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 5 = 2 cm. Count the spaces after 120 cm: 122 cm, 124 cm, 126 cm. So it is 126 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 5 = 2 cm. Count the spaces after 80 cm: 82 cm, 84 cm. So it is 84 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 50 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 cm ÷ 10 = 5 cm. Count the spaces after 200 cm: 205 cm, 210 cm, 215 cm, 220 cm, 225 cm, 230 cm, 235 cm. So it is 235 cm.

items.q: What does the tape measure show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 50 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 cm ÷ 10 = 5 cm. Count the spaces after 150 cm: 155 cm, 160 cm, 165 cm. So it is 165 cm.
The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 10 = 1 cm. Count the spaces after 30 cm: 31 cm, 32 cm, 33 cm, 34 cm, 35 cm, 36 cm, 37 cm. So it is 37 cm.

items.q: A long tape measure is used at the athletics carnival. What does it show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 m = 100 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm, not 1 cm. The pointer is 3 marks past 2 m: 2 m 30 cm.

items.q: A long tape measure is used at the athletics carnival. What does it show at the red pointer?
items.e: The numbers go up by 1 m = 100 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm, not 1 cm. The pointer is 7 marks past 1 m: 1 m 70 cm.

items.q: A ruler is broken, so it starts at 4 cm. A feather goes from the 4 cm mark to the 13 cm mark. How long is the feather?
items.e: It does not start at 0, so take the start away from the end: 13 − 4 = 9 cm.

items.q: A tape measure has the numbers 10, 20, 30, … and 5 spaces between each pair of numbers. What is each mark worth?
items.e: From one number to the next is 10 cm. 10 cm shared into 5 spaces: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 cm.

items.q: Each small mark on a tape measure is worth 5 cm. A line ends 3 marks past 40 cm. Where does it end?
items.e: Count on 3 marks of 5 cm from 40: 45, 50, 55. It ends at 55 cm.

sets.title: Kitchen and bathroom scales: g and kg

items.q: How many grams are in half a kilogram?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Half of 1000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bunch of grapes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 200 g: 250 g. So it is 250 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 600 g: 650 g. So it is 650 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a tub of yoghurt. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 800 g: 850 g. So it is 850 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 250 g: 300 g, 350 g. So it is 350 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 500 g: 550 g, 600 g. So it is 600 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of oranges. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 750 g: 800 g, 850 g, 900 g. So it is 900 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a pineapple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 500 g ÷ 5 = 100 g. Count the spaces after 1000 g: 1100 g, 1200 g, 1300 g. So it is 1300 g.

items.q: The needle is halfway between two marks. What is the mass of the bag of flour?
items.e: Each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is halfway between 400 g and 500 g. Halfway between them is 450 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of potting mix. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 3 × 250 = 750 g. So it is 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a watermelon. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 1 × 500 = 500 g. So it is 3 kg 500 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 8 marks past 1 kg: 8 × 100 = 800 g. So it is 1 kg 800 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 1 mark past 4 kg: 1 × 250 = 250 g. So it is 4 kg 250 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 6 marks past 2 kg: 6 × 100 = 600 g. So it is 2 kg 600 g.

items.q: Jack stands on the bathroom scales. What is his mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 kg ÷ 5 = 1 kg. Count the spaces after 30 kg: 31 kg, 32 kg, 33 kg. So it is 33 kg.

items.q: Mia stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 kg ÷ 5 = 2 kg. Count the spaces after 30 kg: 32 kg, 34 kg, 36 kg. So it is 36 kg.

items.q: Mum stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 20 kg. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 20 kg ÷ 4 = 5 kg. Count the spaces after 40 kg: 45 kg, 50 kg, 55 kg. So it is 55 kg.

items.q: Leo stands on the bathroom scales. What is his mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 kg ÷ 10 = 1 kg. Count the spaces after 20 kg: 21 kg, 22 kg, 23 kg, 24 kg, 25 kg, 26 kg, 27 kg. So it is 27 kg.

items.q: Sienna stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: From 30 kg to 35 kg there are 10 spaces, so each mark is 5000 g ÷ 10 = 500 g, not 1 kg. The pointer is 5 marks past 30 kg: 5 × 500 g = 2500 g = 2 kg 500 g. 30 kg + 2 kg 500 g = 32 kg 500 g.

items.q: Kitchen scales have a mark every 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg. What is the mass?
items.e: Each mark is 250 g, not 1 g. 3 marks: 250, 500, 750. So it is 1 kg 750 g.

sets.title: Jugs with partial marks: mL and L

items.q: A jug has a line every 250 mL. How many spaces are there from 0 up to 1 L?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1000. That is 4 spaces. Do not count the 0 line as a space.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mL ÷ 4 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 200 mL: 250 mL, 300 mL, 350 mL. So it is 350 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mL ÷ 4 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 600 mL: 650 mL. So it is 650 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mL ÷ 5 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 250 mL: 300 mL, 350 mL, 400 mL. So it is 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mL ÷ 5 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 750 mL: 800 mL, 850 mL. So it is 850 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mL ÷ 4 = 25 mL. Count the spaces after 100 mL: 125 mL, 150 mL, 175 mL. So it is 175 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mL ÷ 4 = 25 mL. Count the spaces after 300 mL: 325 mL. So it is 325 mL.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mL. The water is halfway between 500 mL and 600 mL. Halfway is 550 mL.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mL. The water is halfway between 200 mL and 300 mL. Halfway is 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 1 L: 1 × 250 = 250 mL. So it is 1 L 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1 L: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. So it is 1 L 750 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 10 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 mL. The water is 4 lines above 1 L: 4 × 100 = 400 mL. So it is 1 L 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 mL. The water is 1 line above 2 L: 1 × 500 = 500 mL. So it is 2 L 500 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 2 L: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. So it is 2 L 750 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 5 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 5 = 200 mL. The water is 3 lines up from the bottom: 3 × 200 = 600 mL. It has not reached 1 L.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 250 mL, so the water is at 1 L 750 mL. One more line reaches 2 L. So 250 mL more is needed.

items.q: Cooper pours in 150 mL more water. How much water will be in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 50 mL, so the water is at 350 mL now. Pouring in means add: 350 + 150 = 500 mL.

items.q: Which amount is the same as 1500 mL?
A jug has lines every 250 mL. The water is halfway between the 500 mL line and the 1 L line. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: From 500 mL to 1000 mL is 500 mL. Half of 500 is 250. 500 + 250 = 750 mL.

items.q: A jug has a line every 100 mL. The water is 4 lines above 1 L. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL, not 1 mL. 4 × 100 = 400 mL. So it is 1 L 400 mL.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show in the classroom?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 degrees. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 degrees ÷ 10 = 1 degree. Count the spaces after 20 °C: 21 °C, 22 °C, 23 °C. So it is 23 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show on an autumn afternoon?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 degrees. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 degrees ÷ 5 = 1 degree. Count the spaces after 15 °C: 16 °C, 17 °C. So it is 17 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show on a hot day in Sydney?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 degrees. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 degrees ÷ 5 = 2 degrees. Count the spaces after 30 °C: 32 °C, 34 °C. So it is 34 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show at the beach?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 degrees. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 degrees ÷ 5 = 2 degrees. Count the spaces after 20 °C: 22 °C, 24 °C, 26 °C. So it is 26 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show on a summer afternoon in Perth?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 degrees. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 degrees ÷ 5 = 1 degree. Count the spaces after 35 °C: 36 °C, 37 °C, 38 °C. So it is 38 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show on a winter morning in Melbourne?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 degrees. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 degrees ÷ 5 = 1 degree. Count the spaces after 5 °C: 6 °C, 7 °C, 8 °C. So it is 8 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show on a frosty morning?
items.e: The red line ends before 0, so the temperature is below zero. Count back from 0: 2 marks of 1 degree. It is −2 °C, not 2 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: Each mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 degrees. The red line ends 2 marks before 0: 2 × 2 = 4. It is below zero, so it is −4 °C.

items.q: Which temperature is the coldest?
items.e: Temperatures below zero are colder than 0 °C. −2 °C is 2 degrees below zero, so it is the coldest.

items.q: Which temperature is 2 degrees below zero?
items.e: Below zero temperatures have a minus sign. 2 degrees below zero is written −2 °C. 2 °C is 2 degrees above zero.

items.q: It is 3 °C in the evening. Overnight the temperature drops by 5 degrees. What is it now?
items.e: Count down 5 degrees from 3: 2, 1, 0, −1 °C, −2 °C. It goes below zero, so it is −2 °C, not 2 °C.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 2 marks past 15: 15 + 2 = 17 seconds.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 3 marks past 40: 40 + 3 = 43 seconds.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 3 marks past 25: 25 + 3 = 28 seconds.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 2 marks past 50: 50 + 2 = 52 seconds.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 1 mark past 35: 35 + 1 = 36 seconds.
The numbers go up by 5 seconds, and each small mark is 1 second. The hand is 4 marks past 5: 5 + 4 = 9 seconds.

items.q: The digital stopwatch shows minutes and seconds. How long does it show?
items.e: On a stopwatch the number before the colon is minutes and the number after it is seconds. 01:25 is 1 min 25 s, not 1 hour.

items.q: How long does the digital stopwatch show?
items.e: Minutes come before the colon and seconds after it. 02:05 is 2 min 5 s. 05 is 5 seconds, not 50.

items.q: How many seconds altogether does the stopwatch show?
items.e: 01:30 is 1 min 30 s. 1 min = 60 s, so 60 + 30 = 90 s. It is not 130 s, because 1 minute is 60 seconds, not 100.

sets.title: Compare measures and solve word problems

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 500 g = 1500 g and 1 kg 50 g = 1050 g. 1500 g is the most. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 1450.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1 m 20 cm = 120 cm and 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm. 150 cm is the longest.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 L 250 mL = 1250 mL and 1 L 50 mL = 1050 mL. 1500 mL is the most.
Each mark is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. A shows 2 kg 750 g and B shows 3 kg 250 g. B is heavier. From 2 kg 750 g to 3 kg is 250 g, and to 3 kg 250 g is 250 g more: 500 g.

items.q: Which list goes from the coldest to the warmest?
items.e: Below zero is colder than 0 °C. −2 °C is the coldest, then 0 °C, then 3 °C.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Ruby’s stopwatch shows 00:58. Kai’s stopwatch shows 01:02. Who is faster, and by how much?
items.e: 00:58 is 58 s. 01:02 is 1 min 2 s = 62 s. The smaller time is faster, so Ruby wins. 62 − 58 = 4 s.

items.q: On a winter morning in Canberra it is −2 °C at 7 am. By 2 pm it is 12 °C. How many degrees warmer is it at 2 pm?
items.e: Count up from −2 °C to 0: 2 degrees. Then 0 to 12: 12 degrees. 2 + 12 = 14 degrees.

items.q: On a summer day in Perth it is 38 °C at 3 pm. At midnight it is 21 °C. How many degrees cooler is it at midnight?
items.e: Cooler means find the difference: 38 − 21 = 17 degrees. Check: 21 + 17 = 38.

items.q: Mum stands on the bathroom scales: 62 kg. Then she picks up the dog and the scales show 71 kg. What is the mass of the dog?
items.e: The dog’s mass is the difference: 71 − 62 = 9 kg.

items.q: The school canteen buys 2 kg 500 g of onions for the sausage sizzle. They use 1 kg 750 g. How much is left?
items.e: Change to grams: 2500 − 1750 = 750 g. Do not take 500 from 750: the grams part needs regrouping.

items.q: A jug holds 1 L 500 mL of cordial. Six cups of 200 mL are poured for a picnic. How much cordial is left in the jug?
At the athletics carnival, Lachlan jumps 2 m 45 cm and Isla jumps 2 m 70 cm. How much further does Isla jump?
items.e: The metres are the same, so compare the centimetres: 70 − 45 = 25 cm.

items.q: Kai’s pencil is 14 cm 5 mm long. Zara’s pencil is 12 cm 8 mm long. How much longer is Kai’s pencil?
items.e: Change to millimetres: 145 − 128 = 17 mm = 1 cm 7 mm. Do not take 5 from 8 the wrong way round: regroup 1 cm as 10 mm.

items.q: Leo runs 3 laps of the oval. Each lap takes 40 s. How long does he run altogether?
items.e: 3 × 40 = 120 s. 60 s = 1 min, so 120 s = 2 min. 1 min 20 s is wrong: 1 minute is 60 s, not 100 s.

items.q: The kitchen scales show 450 g of flour. The Anzac biscuit recipe needs 1 kg. How much more flour is needed?
The pool must be at least 26 °C for the swimming carnival. How many degrees warmer does the water need to be?
items.e: The thermometer shows 23 °C: each mark is 1 degree and the red line is 3 marks past 20. 26 − 23 = 3 degrees.

items.q: A sunflower in the school garden is measured with a tape measure. How much more must it grow to be 2 m tall?
items.e: Each mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 cm. The pointer is 3 marks past 170: 176 cm. 2 m = 200 cm. 200 − 176 = 24 cm.

items.q: A watering can holds 9 L. A jug holds 1 L 500 mL. How many full jugs fill the watering can?
items.e: Count by 1 L 500 mL: 1 L 500 mL, 3 L, 4 L 500 mL, 6 L, 7 L 500 mL, 9 L. That is 6 jugs.

items.q: A bunch of bananas has a mass of 1 kg 200 g. Another bunch has a mass of 950 g. What is their total mass?
items.e: Change to grams: 1200 + 950 = 2150 g = 2 kg 150 g.

items.q: Charlotte has 1 m of ribbon. She cuts off a 35 cm piece and a 40 cm piece. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. She cuts 35 + 40 = 75 cm. 100 − 75 = 25 cm left.
